title: "Applied Machine Learning and Deep Learning"
subtitle: "Supervised estimation, unsupervised segmentation and generative networks"
---

A portfolio of machine learning and deep learning models spanning supervised estimation, unsupervised segmentation and generative neural networks. Built for the Machine Learning course (Aprendizaje Automático, 2025-26) of the Computer Science and Mathematics double degree at the University of Granada.

[View source on GitHub](https://github.com/laurasalop03/applied-ml-and-deep-learning){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}

## What it covers

**Supervised learning**

- Multi-class classification and continuous regression, applied to predicting hardware pricing and concrete compressive strength.
- Emphasis on feature engineering and mitigating multicollinearity.

**Unsupervised learning**

- K-Means clustering for customer segmentation.
- Association rule mining to map transactional dependencies in market basket data.

**Deep learning (vision and language)**

- Convolutional autoencoders that isolate signal from Gaussian noise in images.
- Dense neural networks (MLP) for binary sentiment analysis of variable length text.

## Engineering highlights

- **Hyperparameter optimization**: manual grid search over learning rates, batch sizes and network depth, balancing model capacity against early overfitting.
- **Data sanitization**: interquartile range (IQR) outlier removal and `StandardScaler` normalization, to keep distance based clustering meaningful and gradient descent stable.

## Why it is relevant to quant work

Return prediction is regression, regime and client segmentation are clustering, and denoising autoencoders are a direct analogue of separating signal from noise in financial series. The discipline shown here, careful feature engineering, outlier handling and honest overfitting control, is exactly what quant modelling demands.

## Tech

Python, TensorFlow, Keras, scikit-learn, NumPy, Pandas.
